glosses: A wrinkling of the forehead with the eyebrows brought together, typically indicating displeasure, severity, or concentration.

examples.text: Philip had once told him of a man who had a horse-shoe frown, and Tom had tried with all his frowning-might to make a horse-shoe on his forehead
He encounters some obstacle in his train of reasoning ... and then a frown passes like a shadow over his brow.

glosses: A downturn of the corners of the mouth, typically expressing sadness.

examples.text: The smile and the frown are both indicated and the operation of a motor driven flasher causes the face to look happy and sad in turn.

glosses: Any facial expression that indicates disapproval or displeasure.
To have a frown on one's face.

examples.text: She frowned when I told her the news.

glosses: To manifest displeasure or disapprobation; to look with disfavour or threateningly.

examples.text: Noisy gossip in the library is frowned upon.
The sky doth frown and lower upon our army.

glosses: To repress or repel by expressing displeasure or disapproval; to rebuke with a look.

examples.text: Let us frown the impudent fellow into silence.
Frank frowned his displeasure with my proposal.
As the band paused between songs, a gust of wind blew a distinctive Worthy Farm odour in the direction of drummer/vocalist Julien Ehrich: “Wow,” he frowned, “this place smells of cow shit.”
